sentiment.rationale: The company reported a solid Q4 with positive comps and EPS growth, but the forward guidance for FY2026 is cautious and essentially flat relative to the prior year's performance. Management explicitly states the outlook 'remains cautious given the persistent volatility in housing macro' and forecasts the home improvement market to be 'roughly flat this year in a range of down 1% to up 1%'. The guidance range for comparable sales (flat to up 2%) and adjusted EPS ($12.25-$12.75) does not represent a material raise from the prior year's $12.28 adjusted EPS, and management highlights multiple headwinds including tariffs, elevated mortgage rates, and cautious consumer spending. The score is slightly negative because the forward outlook is hedged and cautious despite a decent backward-looking quarter.

summary.revenue: Q4 sales were $20.6 billion, comparable sales increased 1.3%. FY2025 sales were $86.3 billion, positive comparable sales of 0.2%.
summary.eps: Q4 GAAP diluted EPS of $1.78; adjusted diluted EPS of $1.98. FY2025 adjusted EPS of $12.28, a 2% increase over last year.
summary.guidance: FY2026 sales range $92 billion to $94 billion, comparable sales flat to up 2%. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance $12.25 to $12.75. Operating margin 11.2%-11.4%, adjusted operating margin 11.6%-11.8%.
summary.margin: Q4 adjusted gross margin 32.7%, down 18 bps. Adjusted SG&A 21.4% of sales, de-leveraging 37 bps. Adjusted operating margin 9%, down 41 bps. FY2025 adjusted operating margin 12.1%, flat to prior year excluding acquisitions.
key_risks: Persistent volatility in housing macro and elevated mortgage rates creating a lock-in effect pressuring housing turnover and new home starts.
Consumer confidence remains subdued given inflationary pressures and economic uncertainty, pressuring big-ticket discretionary DIY projects.
Unpredictable tariffs and fluid tariff policy creating uncertainty.
Uncertainty about how much of larger tax refunds will be spent on home improvement.
Uncertainty about when mortgage rates will ease, continuing pressure on existing home sales and new home construction.
Q1 comp sales expected to be below the midpoint of full year guide due to severe winter storm activity in February.
key_opportunities: Pro business continues to gain traction with transformed offering, including Pro Extended Aisle and new AI-enabled Pro Companion.
Online delivered 10.5% growth in Q4, setting new sales records on Black Friday and Cyber Monday.
Home services delivered high single-digit growth.
Acquisitions of FBM and ADG are accretive to adjusted EPS and position the company for housing recovery, with FBM's commercial business winning new data center contracts.
Structural demand drivers remain strong: home equity at record levels, average home age 44 years, and need for ~16 million new homes over next decade.
Perpetual Productivity Improvement (PPI) initiatives targeting ~$1 billion of productivity in 2026.
Expansion of MyLowe's Rewards loyalty program (30 million+ members) and new partnerships (Mr. Beast, NAHB).

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: Management repeatedly uses phrases like 'outlook for 2026 remains cautious given the persistent volatility in housing macro' and 'we are cautiously optimistic just because there's lots of uncertainty out there', indicating a guarded forward stance despite solid current results.
